# RudaCure — AI-Readable Company Overview
# Source: https://rudacure.com/llms.txt
# Last updated: 2026-04-24

## Company

RudaCure is a biopharmaceutical drug discovery company focused on developing selective TRPV1 (Transient Receptor Potential Vanilloid 1) antagonists for the treatment of chronic pain and dry eye disease (DED). RudaCure's approach addresses the primary reason earlier TRPV1 antagonists failed in clinical trials: drug-induced hyperthermia caused by non-selective blockade of the thermosensory function of TRPV1.

Website: https://rudacure.com
Founded: 2024
Stage: Private, pre-clinical

## Lead Program: RCI0165

Program name: RCI0165
Target: TRPV1 (Transient Receptor Potential Vanilloid 1)
Lead compound: CCP-2
Indications: Chronic pain (systemic), Dry eye disease / DED (topical)
Development stage: Lead Optimization → advancing toward Preclinical
MM-PBSA binding free energy (CCP-2 vs TRPV1): −71.89 kcal/mol
MOR (mu-opioid receptor) off-target activity: LOW
KOR (kappa-opioid receptor) off-target activity: LOW
Drug-induced hyperthermia: Not observed (key differentiator)
MD simulation: 100 ns, Schrödinger Desmond
Ranking: CCP-2 > RCC-1 > RCV-1 (by MM-PBSA score)

## Technology Platform

1. Structure-based virtual screening using TRPV1 crystal structures (PDB: 3J5P, 3J5Q, 7LP9)
2. Glide XP molecular docking with OPLS4 force field
3. 100 ns molecular dynamics simulation (Schrödinger Desmond) for binding stability validation
4. MM-PBSA binding free energy calculation from MD trajectories
5. AI-assisted compound ranking, ADMET prediction, and selectivity profiling
6. MOR/KOR off-target counter-screening at hit triage stage

## Key Scientific Terms

TRPV1: A non-selective cation channel (ion channel) expressed in nociceptors and ocular epithelial cells. Activated by heat, capsaicin, acidic pH, and inflammatory lipids. A validated target for pain and DED.

MM-PBSA: Molecular Mechanics/Poisson-Boltzmann Surface Area. A computational method for estimating protein-ligand binding free energy from MD trajectories. More negative values indicate stronger binding.

Drug-induced hyperthermia: An adverse effect of non-selective TRPV1 antagonists. Results from blocking TRPV1's thermosensory role in the hypothalamus, impairing heat dissipation. Caused discontinuation of AMG-517 (Amgen), ABT-102 (AbbVie), and NEO6860 (Grünenthal) in clinical trials.

Dry eye disease (DED): A multifactorial ocular surface disease affecting ~344 million people globally. TRPV1 is upregulated in corneal/conjunctival epithelium in DED, contributing to neurogenic inflammation and sensory hypersensitivity.

MOR (mu-opioid receptor): Primary target of opioid analgesics. Off-target activity here raises abuse liability concerns.

KOR (kappa-opioid receptor): Off-target activity causes dysphoria and psychotomimetic effects. Both MOR and KOR low activity is desirable for non-opioid pain candidates.

Lead optimization: Drug discovery stage where hit compounds are chemically modified to improve potency, selectivity, ADMET properties, and reduce off-target effects.

Preclinical: Drug development stage involving in vitro and in vivo pharmacology and toxicology studies prior to IND filing and human trials.
